Goal: I can relate a circumscribed angle to its central angle.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A circumscribed angle has its two sides tangent to a circle.

Theorem: two tangent segments from an outside point P are equal. A circumscribed angle is supplementary to the central angle that intercepts the same arc.

Proof: with tangents PA and PB and center O, angles OAP and OBP are right (10.3). Triangles OAP and OBP are congruent by HL, so PA = PB. Quadrilateral OAPB is a kite whose angles add to 360, so angle P + angle AOB = 360 − 90 − 90 = 180.
